title: Bank of America Doubles Down On Chewy After 27% Stock Drop
detail:
Bank of America Doubles Down On Chewy After 27% Stock Drop
Moz Farooque ACCA
Thu, September 3, 2026 at 4:24 PM CDT 2 min read
CHWY
BAC

Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Chewy (NYSE:CHWY) heads into its September 9 earnings report with Bank of America arguing that the beaten-down pet retailer may be approaching a better setup than its stock price suggests.

BofA analyst Michael McGovern reiterated a Buy rating and $31 price target, pointing to improving pet-industry spending trends and continued opportunities for Chewy to expand margins through advertising, healthcare services and automation.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with CHWY.

Is CHWY fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Net/net, we remain constructive on steady compounding earnings growth driven by margin expansion from ads, Health/CVC, & automation/AI, McGovern said.

The bullish call comes after a difficult year for shareholders. Chewy stock has fallen roughly 27% year to date, hurt by a full-year guidance reduction in June and concerns that consumer uncertainty could slow discretionary pet spending.

Wall Street expects fiscal Q2 earnings of $0.18 per share, representing roughly 29% year-over-year growth, on revenue of about $3.32 billion, up approximately 7.1%.

Bank of America sees some encouraging signs underneath those estimates.

The bank's credit- and debit-card data showed pet-industry spending growth accelerating from roughly 1% in Q2 to 2% in July. Separate Second Measure data also indicated improving momentum during July, potentially giving Chewy a better backdrop heading into the quarter.

That matters because investor sentiment has become increasingly divided. Bulls expect pet demand to recover as household formation and premiumization improve, while bears remain focused on slower sales growth and Chewy's market-share trajectory.

McGovern argues the recent valuation reset reflects macroeconomic weakness more than deterioration in Chewy's competitive position.

What Chewy investors should watch next

The September 9 report will largely come down to whether improving category data is beginning to show up in Chewy's actual results.

Investors should watch net sales growth, active customers, Autoship penetration and gross margin, along with management's full-year outlook.

Margin expansion may prove especially important. If advertising, healthcare and automation allow earnings to grow faster than revenue, Chewy could continue compounding profits even while the broader pet category remains subdued.

But another guidance reduction or signs of further market-share pressure would reinforce the bear case.

For now, Bank of America is betting that Chewy's 27% decline has created a more attractive entry point just as industry demand begins showing early signs of improvement.

title: Bank of America's new warning should concern stock investors
detail:
Bank of America's new warning should concern stock investors
Damilola Esebame
Thu, September 3, 2026 at 11:47 AM CDT 5 min read
^GSPC
BAC
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The S&P 500 has delivered double-digit gains in 2026, and the rally has outlasted every warning thrown at it so far. One of Wall Street's most closely tracked positioning gauges is now flashing a different signal.

Bank of America's proprietary Bull & Bear Indicator has remained in sell-signal territory since May 2026, with July weekly readings ranging from 9.5 to 9.6 on a 10-point scale, Business Insider showed. 

Those are the highest levels seen since 2021, driven by extreme positioning across hedge funds, fund managers, equity flows, and credit-market technicals.

"Extreme bull positioning says reduce risk exposure," Bank of America chief investment strategist Michael Hartnett said in a client note, Business Insider reported.

The signal does not guarantee a decline, and prior sell triggers have sometimes fizzled without producing meaningful losses. But the buyer pool has thinned enough that even modest earnings or policy disappointment can spark outsized selling pressure.

Bank of America's indicator hits 9.5 as positioning extremes spread across asset classes

The indicator blends institutional positioning, equity and bond flows, global stock-index breadth, and credit-market technicals into one composite score. When that score crosses above 8.0, the firm treats it as a contrarian sell signal for risk assets.

Fund-manager positioning reached the 99th percentile, equity flows hit the 93rd percentile, and hedge-fund exposure registered at the 83rd percentile in Bank of America's component breakdown reported by Guru Focus. 

Also read: Rare volatility signal prompts stock market alert from 43-year veteran analyst

Credit-market technicals also came in elevated at the 77th percentile, reflecting tight high-yield spreads and thin risk premiums across global bond markets.

A second threshold fired alongside the indicator, with managers cutting cash reserves to 3.5% of total assets under management in the August Global Fund Manager Survey, down from 3.6% in July and the sixth-lowest reading in the survey's history since 1998. 

That breaches Bank of America's 4.0% Cash Rule, a sell indicator that confirms institutions are fully deployed, with almost no dry powder remaining.

What 17 prior sell signals reveal about near-term stock returns

The indicator has fired 17 sell signals since its launch 24 years ago, giving investors a meaningful sample of post-signal outcomes to evaluate.

Global stocks, as measured by the MSCI All Country World Index, averaged declines of 2% to 3% in the two to three months following each signal, Hartnett noted.

Credo Technology Group (CRDO) stock is heading toward its worst week in nearly two years as Wall Street analysts cut their price targets following the company's fiscal first-quarter (Q1) 2027 results. JPMorgan Flags Credo's Optical Ramp Risks

JPMorgan reduced Credo's price target to $310 from $335 while maintaining an 'Overweight' rating, still implying an 87% upside to the stock's last closing price. The firm said Credo's Q1 results showed healthy momentum across its copper and optical product lines, but warned that the company's higher expectations could fall short, particularly around the pace of its optical business expansion.

Bank of America also cut its price target to $275 from $340 while retaining a 'Buy' rating. The firm expects Credo's business mix to gradually move away from active electrical cables, or AECs, and increasingly toward optical products. BofA believes that transition could provide a growth opportunity for the company through fiscal 2027-29.

Rosenblatt Raises CRDO's Price Target

Meanwhile, Rosenblatt raised its price target for Credo Technology to $235 from $215 while keeping a 'Neutral' rating. After Credo's Q1 results, the firm raised its earnings estimates for fiscal 2027 and 2028. However, it wants to see more evidence that ZF Optics and Dust Photonics PIC revenue can grow as expected before becoming more positive.

Credo supplies high-speed connectivity solutions used in data-center infrastructure, making its optical products particularly relevant as demand for AI computing capacity expands.

Credo Technology delivered better-than-expected Q1 results, with adjusted earnings and revenue beating forecasts. Revenue more than doubled from last year, while net income jumped 140% to a record $236.3 million.

title: Bank of America resets Microsoft stock price target for 2026
detail:
Bank of America resets Microsoft stock price target for 2026
Moz Farooque
Wed, September 2, 2026 at 7:37 PM CDT 6 min read
MSFT
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Microsoft's (MSFT) 2026 was bumpy to say the least. 

Shares are up around 3.6% year-to-date and nearly 13% over the past three months, according to Seeking Alpha. However, those gains hide what's been a bruising spring selloff and a relatively strong August rebound.

That said, Bank of America has now revamped its Microsoft stock target, suggesting the year's biggest move might still lie ahead. 

Microsoft wrapped up its fiscal 2026 with quarterly sales of $90 billion, up 18%, while Azure grew 43%. At the same time, Microsoft 365 Copilot also shot up from 20 million paid seats earlier in the year to more than 30 million, solidifying its case as a standalone growth engine.

Still, the company is preparing to unveil its Maia 300 AI chip as early as September, according to Reuters. The company has discussed securing capacity for over 300,000 chips in 2027, with longer-term ambitions above one million.

Yet Microsoft isn't abandoning Nvidia, as its first production Vera Rubin systems arrived in August. 

Against that growing AI footprint, BofA's reset sits above Wall Street's average and perhaps the most intriguing bit was what compelled the bank that Microsoft deserves a richer valuation.

BofA sees Azure execution unlocking $600 valuation

Bank of America analyst Tal Liani bumped his Microsoft price target to $600 from $500 and reiterated a Buy rating. Against a Sept. 1 reference price of $507.29, the target points to a sizeable 18.3% upside. 

For perspective, TipRanks rates BofA's Tal Liani as a top analyst, with a 100% success rate across seven ratings on Microsoft, producing an impressive 24.43% average return. 

The big change is that BofA is now applying a far richer 28-times forecasted calendar-2027 earnings, up substantially from 24 times previously and above its 18-to-25-times software peer range.

Essentially, BofA sees far less execution risk around Microsoft's massive AI investment. 

For some color, Azure was on fire in its recent quarter, posting 39% growth in fiscal Q3 to 43% in Q4, with management guiding to 45% in Q1 2027, soaring above Wall Street's initial 40.6% expectation.

Related: JPMorgan set a serious Microsoft stock price target for 2027

As AI demand still comfortably exceeds available capacity, deploying infrastructure more quickly converts constrained demand into sales instead of merely adding idle assets. BofA consequently models Azure constant-currency growth rising from 39.9% in fiscal 2026 to 41.8% in 2027.

Moreover, the visibility behind that forecast is also equally important. Remaining performance obligations jumped 84% to $678 billion, which creates a substantial contracted-revenue reservoir.

title: Goldman Sachs and BofA Are Making a Major Stablecoin Bet. Is It Worth Watching?

The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) and Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) are among 21 financial institutions planning to launch a U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin in the first half of 2027. The banks are expected to create a joint company to issue the stablecoin, with plans to eventually expand into other G7 currencies, including the euro. The initiative reflects growing interest among traditional banks in blockchain-based payments and could help them compete with established stablecoin issuers.

The opportunity, however, is still developing. Reuters noted that existing bank-issued stablecoins have seen limited adoption, while established players such as Tether continue to dominate the market. That means the project could take years to become financially meaningful for participating banks.

Goldman Sachs and BofA Are Making a Major Stablecoin Bet. Is It Worth Watching?

Photo by Akshay Sadarangani on Unsplash

Goldman Sachs- Bull & Bear Case

The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) could benefit from getting an early foothold in the rapidly developing digital-assets and blockchain ecosystem. The bank's institutional client base and expertise in trading and capital markets could provide several opportunities if stablecoins become more widely used for payments, settlement, and other financial transactions. Rather than simply issuing a digital token, Goldman could potentially build additional financial services around the stablecoin as adoption grows.

The joint structure is also a positive because Goldman will not have to bear the entire cost of developing the infrastructure on its own. Having 20 other major financial institutions involved could create a broader network and make the stablecoin more useful to institutional customers.

The biggest risk is weak adoption. Stablecoins have gained significant traction in crypto markets, but bank-issued alternatives have yet to demonstrate comparable demand. Reuters reported that Societe Generale's dollar-backed stablecoin had only around $12.5 million in circulation, compared with more than $180 billion for Tether.

The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) could therefore end up investing in infrastructure that produces limited revenue. There is also significant competition from established stablecoin issuers and other financial institutions developing their own digital-payment solutions. Regulatory uncertainty adds another layer of risk. As a result, the project is unlikely to have a material impact on Goldman's earnings in the near term.

Bank of America- Bull & Bear Case

Bank of America Corporation (NYSE:BAC) could have a particularly strong use case for a bank-backed stablecoin because of its large payments and commercial-banking operations. If companies increasingly use stablecoins to move money, especially across borders, BofA could integrate the technology into its existing relationships with corporate and institutional clients.

title: Goldman Sachs, BofA Among 21 Banks Planning Joint Dollar Stablecoin Launch
detail:
Goldman Sachs, BofA Among 21 Banks Planning Joint Dollar Stablecoin Launch
Jose Antonio Lanz
Wed, September 2, 2026 at 3:01 PM CDT 2 min read
GS
BAC
DX-Y.NYB
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Twenty-one of the world's largest financial institutions committed Tuesday to build a company that will issue a U.S. dollar stablecoin. Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, and Citi anchor the group, according to a joint statement. The company doesn't have a name yet, and its formation, planned for the second half of 2026, is still subject to closing conditions.

It's worth being precise about what this isn't. A CBDC is a direct liability of a central bank—digital cash the Federal Reserve itself would issue and stand behind. This consortium's token is the opposite: a private liability of a commercial company, backed by reserves the banks hold themselves, with no Fed balance sheet involved.

Myriad: Which company will IPO next? Click to make your prediction.

The distinction has teeth in the U.S. specifically, since President Donald Trump signed an executive order in January 2025 banning federal agencies from developing or issuing a CBDC, while explicitly directing the government to back private, dollar-pegged stablecoins instead. So a bank-issued stablecoin isn't necessarily a backdoor CBDC—it's the exact alternative Washington chose over one.

The roster spans five regions. North America contributes Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, Citi, Capital One, Fidelity Investments, PNC Financial Services, Scotiabank, TD Bank Group, Wells Fargo, and WisdomTree. Europe brings Santander, BBVA, Commerzbank, Crédit Agricole, Deutsche Bank, Lloyds Banking Group, Rabobank, and UBS, while MUFG Bank, Sirius International Holding, and Standard Bank cover East Asia, the Middle East, and Africa.

The banks want the token used across wholesale, institutional, and retail markets, with cross-border payments and digital asset settlement as the first applications. Once the dollar coin ships, a euro-denominated version is next in line, ahead of other G7 currencies. The venture is designed to comply with the U.S. GENIUS Act and, where applicable, the EU's MiCA framework.

The idea isn't new. JPMorgan, Bank of America, Citi, and Wells Fargo have been weighing a joint token since 2025 , months before an initial 10 institutions formally announced the effort. JPMorgan, notably, isn't among the 21 names on this week's list.

The banks aren't the only ones building shared payment rails. In August, 39 state banking trade groups formed the BankChain Alliance, a separate network aimed at giving community and regional lenders access to tokenized deposits. And back in June, Circle's own distribution partners, including Visa, Mastercard, and Stripe, backed Open USD, a rival stablecoin. This caused Circle's stock to drop in response.

Boston Consulting Group and Brunswick Group are advising the venture, though both say they have no authority to bind the consortium or its members. The group's own target remains fixed: a U.S. dollar stablecoin in the market by the first half of 2027.

title: Bank of America (BAC) Stock May Be 31% Undervalued Despite Stablecoin Plans
detail:
Bank of America (BAC) Stock May Be 31% Undervalued Despite Stablecoin Plans
Bailey Pemberton

BAC
DX-Y.NYB
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bank of America stock has delivered a strong 3 year run, yet current valuation checks suggest there may still be a gap between the market price and what an Excess Returns intrinsic value estimate implies. For investors, the key issue is how much weight to place on that potential discount when recent share price moves have been relatively modest.

Bank of America is up 131.3% over the past 3 years, which puts recent short term moves into context as part of a much longer strong period for the stock.

The planned role in a consortium to launch a US dollar stablecoin can support long term fee and payments opportunities. At the same time, ongoing regulatory debates such as the Federal Reserve GSIB capital surcharge revision may limit how much capital the bank can return to shareholders.

With a value score of 3 out of 6, Bank of America shows a mixed picture rather than a clear bargain or clear overvaluation on the broader checks, even though both the Excess Returns intrinsic value estimate and earnings multiples currently screen it as undervalued compared with the share price around US$61.99.

The issue now is whether Bank of America stock still offers enough valuation upside after this multi year run to justify new capital going into the shares.

Spot opportunities that echo Bank of America's valuation story by scanning a curated list of 50 high quality undervalued stocks with solid balance sheets and cash flows.

Is Bank of America a Bargain on Excess Returns?

The Excess Returns model compares profit on shareholders' equity with the cost of that equity to estimate intrinsic value per share for Bank of America. On this view, the bank's Book Value of $39.34 per share and Stable EPS of $5.50 per share, based on analyst return on equity estimates, support an Excess Return of $2.02 per share over a Cost of Equity of $3.48 per share. That is paired with an Average Return on Equity of 12.70% and a Stable Book Value assumption of $43.31 per share.

Combining these inputs, the Excess Returns model indicates an intrinsic value of about $89.95 per share, which is roughly 31.1% above the recent share price around $61.99, so the stock screens as undervalued within this framework. The planned role in a consortium to launch a US dollar stablecoin provides additional context, because it illustrates why the model assumes Bank of America can continue earning returns above its equity cost over time, even while the market prices the stock at a discount to that stream of excess profits.

On these Excess Returns assumptions, Bank of America stock appears undervalued relative to its current trading price.
